title: Zephyrine and the Will
premise: When the coffin of Zephyrine Vale, founder of the tidal town of Marrow's Reach, is exhumed for a centennial ceremony and found empty, true-crime podcaster Freya Joubert is pulled into a mystery older than her show. The town's founding families have guarded a will that names an heir no one has ever met—a witness officially declared dead forty years ago, whose testimony could strip them of everything. As Freya follows tide charts, forged death certificates, and a lighthouse keeper's silence, she realizes the 'accidents' she solved were rehearsals for this cover-up, and that someone in town has been killing to keep the will unread. In the end, the witness—alive, hidden in plain sight as the town archivist—emerges at the spring tide, the will is read aloud on the courthouse steps, and Freya trades her anonymity for a found family among the people she once only observed.
about_author: Hazel Sterling is a former coastal newspaper reporter who spent a decade covering small-town inquests before turning to fiction. She lives within earshot of a working harbor and writes mysteries about the secrets communities keep to survive.

chapters.title: The Exhumation
chapters.summary: Freya Joubert attends the ceremonial exhumation of town founder Zephyrine Vale, recording ambience for her podcast. When the coffin lid opens on empty air, the crowd's grief curdles into fear. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: quiet dread—the moment invisibility ends.

chapters.title: Three Accidents
chapters.summary: Freya reviews her private files on three deaths she quietly proved were murders, all connected to the Vale estate. She never published; now she wonders if her silence made her complicit. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Founding Families
chapters.summary: Freya interviews the four families descended from Zephyrine's partners, cataloguing their polished denials and one nervous slip about 'the reading.' POV: Freya, with interludes from her podcast narration. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt returning.

chapters.title: A Will Nobody Read
chapters.summary: In the county archive, Freya learns Zephyrine's will was sealed pending testimony from a witness listed only by initials: E.M., certified dead since 1984. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: the case acquires a human shape.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: Freya meets Edith Marsh, the soft-spoken town archivist who seems to know which records are missing before Freya asks. Their rapport is immediate and unsettling. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: warmth shadowed by suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Tide Took
chapters.summary: Freya walks the flats at low tide where a 1984 rowboat washed ashore empty, finding a corroded locket engraved with initials that match the witness. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fear—someone else has searched here recently.

chapters.title: Threats in the Dark
chapters.summary: Freya's studio is ransacked; her research drive is gone but nothing valuable taken. A note reads: 'Some cases stay cold for a reason.' POV: Freya. Emotional beat: isolation—the cost of being seen.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Keeper
chapters.summary: Retired keeper Silas Brann tells Freya he saw a woman carried from the water alive in 1984—and that the founding families paid him to forget. POV: alternating Freya and Silas. Emotional beat: a crack of light in forty years of silence.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for Murder
chapters.summary: Freya maps her three solved deaths against the will's timeline and realizes each victim had tried to locate E.M. The pattern isn't coincidence—it's maintenance. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: horror at the scale of the conspiracy.

chapters.title: An Unlikely Ally
chapters.summary: Deputy Cora Ives, whose own father died in one of the 'accidents,' comes to Freya off the record. Together they pull the coroner's sealed files. POV: dual Freya/Cora. Emotional beat: the first stirrings of trust—found family taking root.

chapters.title: The Forged Certificate
chapters.summary: Cora finds the 1984 death certificate bears a signature from a doctor who was out of state that week. The witness was declared dead on paper only. POV: Cora. Emotional beat: righteous anger hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Midnight at the Vale House
chapters.summary: Freya breaks into the shuttered Vale mansion and finds a second, unsealed copy of the will hidden behind Zephyrine's portrait—naming E.M. sole heir to the town's trust. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: triumph immediately punctured by footsteps upstairs.

chapters.title: Caught
chapters.summary: Ambushed by Ambrose Vale, the family patriarch, Freya barely escapes with the will photographed but not secured. He warns her that heirs die before they inherit. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into defiance.

chapters.title: Silas Burns
chapters.summary: Silas's boathouse burns the night after he talks; he survives but recants everything. The message to the town is unmistakable. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grief and shame—the machinery of fear at work.

chapters.title: Following the Money
chapters.summary: Cora traces the trust's disbursements and finds decades of payments routed through a shell company signed 'E. Marsh'—a name used as a shield, not a person. POV: Cora. Emotional beat: confusion deepening the mystery.

chapters.title: The Podcast Goes Live
chapters.summary: Freya publishes the episode she swore she'd never make, laying out the empty coffin, the forged certificate, and the living witness. The town erupts; so do the threats. POV: Freya. Emotional bet: choosing exposure over safety.

chapters.title: Someone Is Watching E.M.
chapters.summary: Freya realizes the shell company's signature block matches handwriting samples from the archive—and that whoever uses the name E.M. has been protecting the real witness for years. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: the puzzle inverting.

chapters.title: The Confession in the Chapel
chapters.summary: Edith Marsh confesses: she faked her own death in 1984 after witnessing Ambrose's grandfather drown Zephyrine's chosen heir, and has hidden ever since, guarding the will. POV: Edith. Emotional beat: forty years of loneliness breaking open.

chapters.title: Before the Tide Turns
chapters.summary: With spring tide approaching—the legal deadline written into the will—Ambrose moves to destroy the original document. Freya, Cora, and Edith race to secure it, ambushed at the Vale house. POV: rotating trio. Emotional beat: desperation and solidarity fused.

chapters.title: The Reading on the Courthouse Steps
chapters.summary: At high tide, before the assembled town, Edith steps forward as E.M.—alive—and the will is read aloud, dissolving the families' hold on the trust. Ambrose is arrested as evidence of his grandfather's crime surfaces. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: catharsis; the coldest case breathing again.

chapters.title: What Stays Buried
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, Freya re-examines Zephyrine's empty coffin and chooses to leave one question unanswered out of mercy for the town. Some mysteries belong to the dead. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: wisdom earned through loss.

chapters.title: Low Tide, New Light
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Freya records her final episode from Edith's kitchen table, surrounded by Cora, Silas, and the town she once watched from outside. The invisible woman has a family now. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: belonging—the tide gives back what it took.
